headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line, and fear is doing the same math as the tape
paragraphs: Start with regime, because it's unanimous today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA all sit below their 200-day moving averages, none showing a golden cross. That's not a mixed market, that's a market still in a downtrend by the slowest, most reliable measure there is. BTC is 49.4% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is down 60.9% from its own peak, and the smaller names are worse: ADA sits 81.8% below its high, DOGE 75.8% below. When everything agrees on direction like this, the story isn't which coin is broken, it's that the whole complex has been marked down together.

Momentum tells a quieter story than the trend does. BTC's RSI at 43.6 and MACD below signal both lean soft but not oversold, more like a market resting than one being sold in a panic. ETH's RSI of 51.6 is roughly neutral even though price sits nowhere near its highs, which is a small divergence worth naming: momentum has stopped falling even as the long-term trend stays negative. SOL, BNB and DOGE all show MACD above signal, a short-term thrust that hasn't yet done anything to their 200-day posture. XRP is the outlier on the soft side, RSI 35.3 and down 3.41% over seven days, closer to actual weakness than the others.

Positioning is where the tension sharpens. BTC funding on OKX is 0.0057% per 8 hours (about 6.3% annualized), a mild cost for holding longs, and the long/short account ratio is 2.27, meaning there are more than two accounts long for every one short. ETH funding runs slightly hotter at 6.4% annualized with a 1.87 ratio. DOGE stands out at 11.0% annualized funding and a long/short ratio of 5.46, a crowded long book by any measure, funding that expensive is longs paying a real toll to stay in the trade. SOL and XRP funding have actually gone negative (-0.4% and -4.2% annualized), shorts paying to hold there, even as their long/short ratios sit at 2.48 and 3.61, more accounts long than short despite the negative funding. That's a genuine mismatch worth sitting with: crowded long by account count, but the marginal money (the futures book) is leaning enough short to flip the funding sign. Liquidations lean toward shorts getting hurt on ETH specifically, $1.09M in short liquidations over 23 hours versus $108K in longs, a one-sided squeeze in that window.

On flows, the picture is cooler than the funding story. BTC spot ETFs printed -$56.2M on 14 Aug 2026, and the five-session net is -$385.2M with three of those days in the same (outflow) direction, a real if modest bid withdrawal from the traditional-finance side. ETH ETFs went the other way, +$5.9M on 13 Aug and +$46.6M over five sessions, though only two days pointed that direction, too thin to call a trend. Whale activity over the last 48 hours shows $62.6M in BTC moving onto exchanges, all of it into Coinbase, net direction labeled 'onto exchanges' in the data, which typically reads as coins positioned closer to potential selling rather than storage. That said, the weekly net series behind it ($445.9M, $1,075.3M, $0.74M, -$441.5M in net outflows from exchanges across the last four weekly readings) shows the trend flipping mid-stream, from strong outflow weeks to a negative (inflow) week most recently, so this isn't a clean multi-week story either way. Stablecoin float is down 0.53% over 30 days to $306.4B, a small drain in dry powder rather than a buildup.

Fear & Greed sits at 34, labeled Fear, and it's actually at the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 34, meaning sentiment has been worse recently than it is right now. That's the crowd feeling slightly less bad while the ETF tape shows outflows and whale coins move toward an exchange. Worth watching from here: whether BTC ETF flows turn positive and stay there for more than a couple of sessions, whether the whale weekly net flips back to outflow (coins leaving exchanges) after this one inflow week, and whether DOGE's stretched funding and 5.46 long/short ratio unwind through funding cooling off or through a liquidation event. Any one of those changing would tell you more about what happens to the trend than the Fear & Greed number does today.
